def: A concise record for a deployed AI system covering its intended use, out-of-scope uses, data and model versions, evaluation results by slice, known limitations, human-oversight design and owners, kept current for reviewers and operators.
eg: Answers stakeholders who ask 'what can this do and where does it fail?' and supports audits.

def: A picture of how data moves through the solution, from sources through prompts, tools, model providers and storage to outputs, marking trust boundaries, sensitive data and retention points.
eg: Security and privacy reviewers ask for it first.

def: Step-by-step operating instructions for a specific situation, such as a burst of 429 errors, a model retirement, a suspected injection or a harmful output, naming who acts, which dashboards to check, how to roll back and whom to notify.
eg: Part of handoff; test it with a drill before launch.

def: A pre-launch checklist review confirming that monitoring and alerts, runbooks, on-call ownership, rollback, capacity, security sign-off, training and support processes are in place before the system goes live.
eg: Often the last phase gate before go-live.

def: A short period right after launch with intensified monitoring, rapid fixes and close contact with users and stakeholders, before the solution moves to normal support.
eg: Staff it with the build team, then hand over steady-state ownership.

def: Managing prompts, templates and model settings as versioned, reviewed, tested artifacts with change history, a release tag recorded on every request and the ability to roll back, instead of editing live text in place.
eg: Without it, a quality drop cannot be traced to a change.

def: The stages Anthropic uses for each model: active (fully supported), legacy (no more updates, may be deprecated), deprecated (still works but not recommended, with a replacement and retirement date) and retired (requests fail). Publicly released models get at least 60 days' notice before retirement.
eg: Partner platforms (Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud) set their own schedules. Audit use with the Console usage export by key and model.

def: A planned move from one model version to another: inventory usage, read the migration notes for rejected parameters, recount tokens, audit prompts, run the evaluation suite side by side, shadow or canary, then cut over with rollback ready, well before the retirement date.
eg: Newer models can reject parameters older code sets and read old prompt wording more literally.

def: A runtime switch that turns a code path, prompt version or model on for chosen users or percentages without redeploying, enabling gradual rollout, quick rollback and separation of deployment from release.
eg: Use it for canary exposure of a new model and as a kill switch for risky behavior.

def: The umbrella name for organization policy in Claude Code that takes precedence over user and project configuration and can lock permissions, MCP servers, plugins, hooks and network destinations, whichever delivery route carries it.
eg: Highest tier of the settings hierarchy. Array settings such as permission rules merge, so developers can add entries but not remove managed ones.

def: Claude Code policy configured in the claude.ai admin console (Teams and Enterprise) and fetched from Anthropic's servers at startup and refreshed hourly, needing no device management. It is a client-side control rather than a security boundary on unmanaged devices.
eg: Setting forceRemoteSettingsRefresh makes clients exit instead of starting without fresh policy.

def: Claude Code policy deployed to devices through MDM profiles, registry policies or a settings file in a protected system directory. Operating-system permissions keep users from editing it, so it gives stronger guarantees than delivery from the cloud.
eg: Among managed sources the order is server-managed, then plist or machine registry policy, then the file, with the user-writable registry lowest.

def: Claude Code rules evaluated in the order deny, then ask, then allow, where the first match decides the outcome. A narrow allow cannot carve an exception out of a broad deny, and the rules are enforced by the tool rather than by the model.
eg: Use them with sandboxing: rules match command text, while the sandbox enforces access at the OS level.

def: Managed-only settings that stop developers from loosening policy, such as making managed settings the sole source of permission rules and disabling the mode that skips permission prompts.
eg: Keys: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly and permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode. Similar locks exist for hooks and MCP servers.

def: Administrator control over which MCP servers Claude Code may use: allowlists and denylists, an option that honors only the managed allowlist, or a deployed managed file that provides a fixed set of servers to every user.
eg: Stops developers from connecting unvetted servers; pair it with plugin marketplace restrictions.

def: Managed settings that restrict which plugin marketplaces developers may add or install from, block sideloading flags and command-based plugin sources, and let administrators distribute vetted plugins, skills and hooks.
eg: Keys include strictKnownMarketplaces and strictPluginOnlyCustomization. Treat plugins like software installs.

def: A managed-policy instruction file placed at a protected system path on each machine, loaded into every Claude Code session and impossible for users to exclude, used for company standards, security policy and compliance rules.
eg: It is guidance only: it shapes behavior but does not enforce. Use permission rules, hooks or sandboxing for rules that must hold.

def: A markdown file Claude Code reads at the start of every session to learn project commands, conventions and gotchas it cannot infer from the code. Keep it short (under about 200 lines), check it into git, and move situational instructions into skills or path-scoped rules.
eg: A bloated file makes Claude ignore parts of it. Running /init generates a starter.

def: User-defined commands that Claude Code runs automatically at lifecycle points, such as before or after a tool call or when a turn ends. Because they run deterministically, they enforce rules (format after edit, block a command, require tests to pass) instead of hoping the model complies.
eg: In a PreToolUse hook, exit code 2 blocks the action. CLAUDE.md is guidance; hooks are guarantees.

def: A dashboard showing adoption and impact: active users and sessions, suggestion accept rate, lines accepted and, on Teams and Enterprise with GitHub connected, merged pull requests that contain Claude-assisted code. Console API customers get usage and spend views.
eg: Contribution metrics are deliberately conservative, unavailable for ZDR organizations, and do not cover usage through cloud providers.

def: Opt-in export of Claude Code metrics (sessions, tokens, cost, lines changed, tool decisions) and events to your own collector, switched on by an environment variable and best pinned in managed settings. Prompt text is redacted unless explicitly enabled.
eg: The only way to stream per-user cost into your own stack in near real time; it works with every provider, including cloud-platform deployments.

def: A proxy that sits between Claude Code (or other clients) and the model provider to centralize credentials, per-user usage tracking, spend limits and request logging, and to route by data sensitivity.
eg: Anthropic offers a self-hosted Claude apps gateway. Sessions that go through any gateway are not eligible for the HIPAA configuration.

def: An adoption approach in which engineers who already use the tool well share reusable prompts and wins in channels the team already reads, answer questions publicly, run a weekly show-and-tell and pair on first tasks, so adoption is carried by habits rather than announcements.
eg: Claude Code's champion kit assumes a modest weekly time budget and offers a thirty-day playbook.

def: Ready-to-adapt launch material for a developer-tool rollout: an organization-wide announcement, an executive-sponsor variant, tips messages and FAQ answers, plus a pre-send checklist (channel created, install tested, data-handling link ready, a named owner, one concrete first task).
eg: Rewrite it in your own voice and swap in real tasks from your codebase.

def: Running Claude Code from scripts, CI jobs and hooks with a prompt flag and no interactive session, with options for allowed tools, turn limits, permission mode and structured output formats, so it can lint, review or triage automatically.
eg: Store credentials as pipeline secrets, cap work with a turn limit, and keep the permission set minimal.

def: A check Claude can run itself and read the result of, such as a test suite, build, linter or screenshot comparison, given in the prompt or enforced by a hook, so work is verified by evidence instead of by the developer eyeballing it.
eg: The difference between a session you watch and one you can leave running.

def: Claude Code's automatic snapshots of files before edits, with each prompt creating a restore point, letting a developer roll back conversation, code or both with a double escape or a slash command. Changes made through shell commands are not captured.
eg: Not a replacement for git; it lets developers try risky approaches cheaply.

def: A Claude Code permission mode in which the agent researches the codebase and proposes changes for approval without editing files, used for complex or risky work and for building trust with new users.
eg: Cheaper than re-work after a wrong direction.

def: A Claude Code permission mode in which a separate classifier model reviews most actions, blocking risky ones such as scope escalation or hostile-content-driven steps while letting routine work proceed without prompts; organizations can turn it off.
eg: Reduces prompt fatigue; explicit deny rules still apply.
